sentences.zh: 【晉紀七】起昭陽大淵獻，盡閼逢困敦，凡二年。

translations.literal: [Jin Annals 7] From Zhaoyang Dayuanxian through Efeng Kundun; two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: [Jin Annals 7] From the year Zhaoyang Dayuanxian through Efeng Kundun—two years in all.

sentences.zh: 孝惠皇帝中之下太安二年（

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaohui, middle section, lower part, second year of Taian (
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui of Jin, middle reign, lower section, second year of Taian (

sentences.zh: 癸亥，公元三零三年）

translations.literal: guihai, AD 303)
translations.idiomatic: guihai, AD 303)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，李特潛渡江擊羅尚，水上軍皆散走。

translations.literal: In spring, the first month, Li Te secretly crossed the river and attacked Luo Shang; the river forces all scattered and fled.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, Li Te secretly crossed the river to attack Luo Shang, and all the government forces on the water scattered and fled.

sentences.zh: 蜀郡太守徐儉以少城降，特入據之，惟取馬以供軍，餘無侵掠，赦其境內，改元建初。

translations.literal: Shu Commandery Prefect Xu Jian surrendered Shaocheng; Te entered and occupied it, taking only horses to supply the army, with no other plundering; he granted amnesty within his territory and changed the era name to Jianchu.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jian, prefect of Shu Commandery, surrendered Shaocheng. Li Te entered and took possession, seizing only horses for his army and plundering nothing else; he proclaimed an amnesty within his domain and adopted the era name Jianchu.

sentences.zh: 羅尚保太城，遣使求和於特。

translations.literal: Luo Shang held Taicheng and sent envoys to seek peace with Te.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang held fast in Taicheng and sent envoys to sue for peace with Li Te.

sentences.zh: 蜀民相聚為塢者，皆送款於特，特遣使就撫之；

translations.literal: Shu people who had gathered into fortified stockades all submitted to Te; Te sent envoys to go and pacify them;
translations.idiomatic: The Shu populace who had banded together in fortified stockades all pledged allegiance to Li Te, and he sent envoys to reassure and win them over;

sentences.zh: 以軍中糧少，乃分六郡流民於諸塢就食。

translations.literal: Because army grain was scarce, he distributed refugees from the six commanderies among the various stockades to obtain food.
translations.idiomatic: With provisions in the army running low, he dispersed refugees from the six commanderies among the stockades to live off local supplies.

sentences.zh: 李流言於特曰：「諸塢新附，人心未固，宜質其大姓子弟，聚兵自守，以備不虞。」

translations.literal: Li Liu said to Te: "The stockades have newly submitted and hearts are not yet firm; you should take the sons of their great clans as hostages, gather troops, and hold yourselves in readiness against the unforeseen."
translations.idiomatic: Li Liu said to Li Te, "These stockades have only just come over, and loyalty is still uncertain. You ought to hold the sons of their leading families as hostages, mass your troops, and stand guard against surprise."

sentences.zh: 又與特司馬上官惇書曰：「納降如待敵，不可易也。」

translations.literal: He also wrote to Te's Major-General Shangguan Dun: "Receiving surrender is like facing an enemy; it must not be taken lightly."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Li Te's major-general Shangguan Dun: "Treat those who surrender as you would an enemy—never let your guard down."

sentences.zh: 前將軍雄亦以為言。

translations.literal: The Forward General Xiong also spoke likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong, the forward general, said the same.

sentences.zh: 特怒曰：「大事已定，但當安民，何為更逆加疑忌，使之離叛乎！」

translations.literal: Te angrily said: "The great affair is already settled; we need only settle the people—why go further and add suspicion and wariness, driving them to rebel!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Te flew into a rage. "The great struggle is won," he said. "All that remains is to reassure the people. Why heap fresh suspicion on them and drive them back into revolt?"

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣荊州刺史宗岱、建平太守孫阜帥水軍三萬以救羅尚。

translations.literal: The court dispatched Jing Province Inspector Zong Dai and Jianping Administrator Sun Fu to lead thirty thousand river troops to rescue Luo Shang.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Zong Dai, inspector of Jing Province, and Sun Fu, administrator of Jianping, to lead thirty thousand river troops to relieve Luo Shang.

sentences.zh: 岱以阜為前鋒，進逼德陽。

translations.literal: Dai made Fu the vanguard and advanced to press Deyang.
translations.idiomatic: Dai placed Sun Fu in the van and pressed toward Deyang.

sentences.zh: 特遣李蕩及蜀郡太守李璜就德陽太守任臧共拒之。

translations.literal: Te sent Li Dang and Shu Commandery Prefect Li Huang to join Deyang Administrator Ren Zang in resisting them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Te sent Li Dang and Li Huang, prefect of Shu Commandery, to join Ren Zang, administrator of Deyang, in the defense.

sentences.zh: 岱、阜軍勢甚盛，諸塢皆有貳志。

translations.literal: Dai and Fu's army momentum was very strong, and all the stockades harbored divided loyalties.
translations.idiomatic: The armies of Dai and Fu were formidable, and every stockade began to waver in its allegiance.

sentences.zh: 益州兵曹從事蜀郡任睿言於羅尚曰：「李特散眾就食，驕怠無備，此天亡之時也。

translations.literal: Yizhou Military Affairs Clerk Shu Commandery Ren Rui said to Luo Shang: "Li Te has dispersed his host to forage; they are arrogant, slack, and unprepared—this is the hour Heaven would destroy them.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Rui of Shu Commandery, a clerk in the Yizhou military bureau, told Luo Shang, "Li Te has scattered his men to live off the stockades. They are arrogant, slack, and off their guard. Heaven itself has opened the moment to destroy them.

sentences.zh: 宜密約諸塢，刻期同發，內外擊之，破之必矣！」

translations.literal: You should secretly arrange with all the stockades, fix a date for a joint rising, strike from within and without, and you will surely break them!"
translations.idiomatic: Secretly concert with every stockade, fix a day for a joint attack, and strike him from within and without. He cannot fail to be broken!"

sentences.zh: 尚使睿夜縋出城，宣旨於諸塢，期以二月十日同擊特。

translations.literal: Shang had Rui lowered by rope from the city by night to proclaim the imperial order to the stockades, fixing the tenth day of the second month for a joint attack on Te.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang had Rui let down from the walls by night on a rope to carry the imperial order to the stockades, setting the tenth day of the second month for a concerted strike against Li Te.

sentences.zh: 睿因詣特詐降。

translations.literal: Rui then went to Te and feigned surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Rui then went to Li Te and pretended to defect.

sentences.zh: 特問城中虛實，睿曰：「糧儲將盡，但餘貨帛耳。」

translations.literal: Te asked about the true state of the city; Rui said: "Grain stores are nearly exhausted; only goods and silks remain."
translations.idiomatic: Li Te asked about conditions in the city. Rui replied, "Grain is almost gone. Only goods and silks are left."

sentences.zh: 睿求出省家，特許之，遂還報尚。

translations.literal: Rui asked leave to visit his family; Te permitted it, and he returned to report to Shang.
translations.idiomatic: He asked permission to visit his family, and Li Te granted it; Rui then went back and reported to Luo Shang.

sentences.zh: 二月，尚遣兵掩襲特營，諸塢皆應之，特兵大敗，斬特及李輔、李遠，皆焚屍，傳首洛陽。

translations.literal: In the second month, Shang sent troops in a surprise attack on Te's camp; all the stockades responded; Te's army was utterly defeated; Te and Li Fu and Li Yuan were beheaded, their corpses burned, and their heads sent to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Luo Shang launched a surprise assault on Li Te's camp. Every stockade rose in answer. Li Te's army was routed; Te himself, with Li Fu and Li Yuan, was killed, the bodies burned, and the heads dispatched to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 流民大懼，李流、李蕩、李雄收餘眾還保赤祖。

translations.literal: The refugees were greatly afraid; Li Liu, Li Dang, and Li Xiong gathered the remnant host and withdrew to hold Chizu.
translations.idiomatic: The refugee host was thrown into panic. Li Liu, Li Dang, and Li Xiong rallied the survivors and fell back to defend Chizu.

sentences.zh: 流自稱大將軍、大都督、益州牧，保東宮，蕩、雄保北營。

translations.literal: Liu styled himself Grand General, Grand Commander-in-Chief, and Governor of Yizhou, holding the Eastern Palace; Dang and Xiong held the Northern Camp.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liu took the titles Grand General, Grand Commander-in-Chief, and Governor of Yizhou, and held the eastern strongpoint; Li Dang and Li Xiong held the northern camp.

sentences.zh: 孫阜破德陽，獲寋碩，任臧退屯涪陵。

translations.literal: Sun Fu broke Deyang, captured Jian Shuo, and Ren Zang withdrew to garrison at Fuling.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Fu took Deyang, captured Jian Shuo, and Ren Zang withdrew to encamp at Fuling.

sentences.zh: 三月，羅尚遣督護何沖、常深等攻李流，涪陵民藥紳等亦起兵攻流。

translations.literal: In the third month, Luo Shang sent Supervisors He Chong and Chang Shen and others to attack Li Liu; Fuling people Yao Shen and others also raised troops to attack Liu.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Luo Shang sent the supervisors He Chong and Chang Shen against Li Liu, while Yao Shen and other men of Fuling also took up arms against him.

sentences.zh: 流與李驤拒深，使李蕩、李雄拒紳。

translations.literal: Liu with Li Xiang resisted Chang Shen; he sent Li Dang and Li Xiong to resist Yao Shen.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liu and Li Xiang met Chang Shen in battle, while Li Dang and Li Xiong were sent to hold off Yao Shen.

sentences.zh: 何沖乘虛攻北營，氐苻成、隗伯在營中，叛應之。

translations.literal: He Chong seized the moment of weakness to attack the Northern Camp; the Di Fu Cheng and Wei Bo were in the camp and rebelled in response.
translations.idiomatic: He Chong struck at an opening and assaulted the northern camp. Fu Cheng of the Di and Wei Bo, who were inside, turned traitor and joined him.

sentences.zh: 蕩母羅氏擐甲拒戰，伯手刃傷其目，羅氏氣益壯；

translations.literal: Dang's mother Lady Luo donned armor to resist in battle; Bo with his own hand wounded her eye, yet Lady Luo's spirit grew only fiercer;
translations.idiomatic: Li Dang's mother, Lady Luo, buckled on armor and fought back. Wei Bo struck her in the eye with his own blade, yet her spirit only burned hotter;

sentences.zh: 營垂破，會流等破深、紳，引兵還，與沖等戰，大破之，成、伯帥其黨突出詣尚。

translations.literal: The camp was on the verge of collapse, when Liu and the others defeated Chang Shen and Yao Shen, led troops back, fought Chong and the rest, and routed them utterly; Cheng and Bo led their faction in a breakout to join Shang.
translations.idiomatic: the camp was near collapse when Li Liu and the others routed Chang Shen and Yao Shen, wheeled about, and fell on He Chong's force, breaking it completely. Fu Cheng and Wei Bo broke out with their followers and fled to Luo Shang.

sentences.zh: 流等乘勝進抵成都，尚復閉城自守。

translations.literal: Liu and the others pressed the victory and advanced to Chengdu; Shang again shut the city and held himself within.
translations.idiomatic: Riding their victory, Li Liu and his brothers pressed on to Chengdu. Luo Shang once more barred the gates and held the city.

sentences.zh: 蕩馳馬逐北，中矛而死。

translations.literal: Dang spurred his horse in pursuit of the fleeing foe and was struck by a spear and died.
translations.idiomatic: Li Dang galloped in pursuit of the retreating enemy and was killed by a spear thrust.

sentences.zh: 朝廷遣侍中燕國劉沈假節統羅尚、許雄等軍，討李流。

translations.literal: The court dispatched Palace Attendant Liu Shen of Yan with credential staff to command the armies of Luo Shang, Xu Xiong, and others to campaign against Li Liu.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent Liu Shen of Yan, a palace attendant bearing the credential staff, to take command of the forces of Luo Shang, Xu Xiong, and others against Li Liu.

sentences.zh: 行至長安，河間王顒留沈為軍師，遣席薳代之。

translations.literal: When he reached Chang'an, Prince of Hejian Yong retained Shen as military adviser and sent Xi Nao to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Chang'an, Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian, kept Liu Shen as his military adviser and sent Xi Nao to take his place.

sentences.zh: 李流以李特、李蕩繼死，宗岱、孫阜將至，甚懼。

translations.literal: Li Liu, because Li Te and Li Dang had died in succession and Zong Dai and Sun Fu were about to arrive, was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liu was deeply alarmed. Li Te and Li Dang were dead in turn, and Zong Dai and Sun Fu were closing in.

sentences.zh: 李含勸流降，流從之；

translations.literal: Li Han urged Liu to surrender, and Liu followed his counsel;
translations.idiomatic: Li Han urged Li Liu to submit, and Liu agreed;

sentences.zh: 李驤、李雄迭諫，不納。

translations.literal: Li Xiang and Li Xiong remonstrated in turn, but he would not heed them.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang and Li Xiong pleaded with him again and again, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 夏，五月，流遣其子世及含子胡為質於阜軍；

translations.literal: In summer, the fifth month, Liu sent his son Shi and Han's son Hu as hostages to Fu's army;
translations.idiomatic: In summer, the fifth month, Li Liu sent his son Shi and Li Han's son Hu as hostages to Sun Fu's camp;

sentences.zh: 胡兄離為梓潼太守，聞之，自郡馳還，欲諫不及。

translations.literal: Hu's elder brother Li was Administrator of Zitong; hearing of it, he galloped back from the commandery, wishing to remonstrate but too late.
translations.idiomatic: Li Li, Hu's elder brother and administrator of Zitong, heard the news and raced back from his post, but arrived too late to dissuade them.

sentences.zh: 退，與雄謀襲阜軍，雄曰：「為今計，當如是；

translations.literal: He withdrew and plotted with Xiong to strike Fu's army; Xiong said: "For the present plan, it ought to be thus;
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew and plotted with Li Xiong to strike Sun Fu's army. Xiong said, "Under the circumstances, that is what we ought to do—

sentences.zh: 而二翁不從，奈何？」

translations.literal: yet the two elders will not follow—what is to be done?"
translations.idiomatic: but the two elders will not hear of it. What can we do?"

sentences.zh: 離曰：「當劫之耳！」

translations.literal: Li said: "We should seize them by force!"
translations.idiomatic: Li Li said, "Then we seize them by force!"

sentences.zh: 雄大喜，乃共說流民曰：「吾屬前已殘暴蜀民，今一旦束手，便為魚肉。

translations.literal: Xiong was greatly pleased, and together they persuaded the refugees: "We have already brutalized the Shu people before; if we now submit and bind our hands, we will become fish on the chopping block.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong was delighted, and together they rallied the refugees: "We have already ravaged the people of Shu. If we now lay down our arms, we will be butchered like fish on a block.

sentences.zh: 惟有同心襲阜，以取富貴耳！」

translations.literal: Only by joining hearts to strike Fu can we win wealth and rank!"
translations.idiomatic: Our only hope is to strike Sun Fu together and win wealth and rank!"

sentences.zh: 眾皆從之。

translations.literal: The host all followed them.
translations.idiomatic: The whole host assented.

sentences.zh: 雄遂與離襲擊阜軍，大破之。

translations.literal: Xiong then with Li launched a surprise attack on Fu's army and routed it utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong and Li Li then fell on Sun Fu's camp and broke it completely.

sentences.zh: 會宗岱卒於墊江，荊州軍遂退。

translations.literal: At the same time Zong Dai died at Dianjiang, and the Jing Province army then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: About the same time Zong Dai died at Dianjiang, and the armies of Jing Province withdrew.

sentences.zh: 流甚慚，由是奇雄才，軍事悉以任之。

translations.literal: Liu was deeply ashamed, and from this marveled at Xiong's talent, entrusting him with all military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liu was deeply ashamed, and from that moment he recognized Li Xiong's genius and entrusted him with all military matters.

sentences.zh: 新野莊王歆，為政嚴急，失蠻夷心，義陽蠻張昌聚黨數千人，欲為亂。

translations.literal: Prince Zhuang of Xinye Xin governed with harsh severity, losing the hearts of the barbarians; Yiyang barbarian Zhang Chang gathered a faction of several thousand men and intended rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xin, Prince Zhuang of Xinye, ruled with harsh severity and lost the loyalty of the tribal peoples. Zhang Chang, a man of the Yiyang tribes, gathered several thousand followers and prepared to rebel.

sentences.zh: 荊州以壬午詔書發武勇赴益州討李流，號「壬午兵」。

translations.literal: Jing Province, by the renwu imperial edict, mobilized fighting men to go to Yizhou to campaign against Li Liu; they were called the "Renwu Troops."
translations.idiomatic: On the strength of the renwu edict, Jing Province mobilized fighting men for an expedition to Yizhou against Li Liu. They were known as the "Renwu troops."

sentences.zh: 民憚遠征，皆不欲行。

translations.literal: The people feared the distant campaign and none wished to go.
translations.idiomatic: The people dreaded the long march and were unwilling to go.

sentences.zh: 詔書督遣嚴急，所經之界停留五日者，二千石免官。

translations.literal: The edict's supervision and dispatch were harshly urgent: wherever the route passed, if men tarried five days, the two-thousand-shi official was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: The edict pressed for swift dispatch with brutal urgency: any district where men lingered five days would see its chief official removed.

sentences.zh: 由是郡縣官長皆親出驅逐；

translations.literal: Because of this, commandery and county heads all went out in person to drive them on;
translations.idiomatic: Commandery and county magistrates therefore went out in person to drive the levies forward;

sentences.zh: 展轉不遠，輒復屯聚為群盜。

translations.literal: having gone only a short distance in circuit, they would again gather and become bandit gangs.
translations.idiomatic: but scarcely had they marched a short distance before the men would gather again and turn to banditry.

sentences.zh: 時江夏大稔，民就食者數千口。

translations.literal: At that time Jiangxia had a great harvest, and several thousand people came seeking food.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangxia had enjoyed a bumper harvest, and several thousand people came there seeking food.

sentences.zh: 張昌因之誑惑百姓，更姓名曰李辰，募眾於安陸石巖山，請流民及避戍役者多往從之。

translations.literal: Zhang Chang took advantage of this to deceive and incite the people, changed his name to Li Chen, and recruited a host at Shiyan Mountain in Anlu; many refugees and those evading corvée went to join him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang seized the opportunity to mislead the populace. He changed his name to Li Chen and raised followers on Shiyan Mountain in Anlu. Refugees and men fleeing corvée duty flocked to him in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 太守弓欽遣兵討之，不勝。

translations.literal: Administrator Gong Qin sent troops to campaign against him and could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Qin, the administrator, sent troops against him but was defeated.

sentences.zh: 昌遂攻郡，欽兵敗，與部將朱伺奔武昌，歆遣騎督靳滿討之，滿覆敗走。

translations.literal: Chang then attacked the commandery; Qin's troops were defeated, and with his subordinate general Zhu Si he fled to Wuchang; Xin sent Cavalry Supervisor Jin Man to campaign against him, and Man was utterly defeated and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang then attacked the commandery seat. Gong Qin's force was broken, and he fled to Wuchang with his lieutenant Zhu Si. Sima Xin sent the cavalry supervisor Jin Man against him, but Jin Man was routed and driven off.

sentences.zh: 昌遂據江夏，造妖言云：「當有聖人出為民主。」

translations.literal: Chang then occupied Jiangxia and fabricated demonic talk, saying: "A sage will appear to be lord of the people."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang seized Jiangxia and spread sorcerous rumors: "A sage will arise to rule the people."

sentences.zh: 得山都縣吏丘沈，更其姓名曰劉尼，詐雲漢後，奉以為天子，曰：「此聖人也。」

translations.literal: He obtained Shandu County clerk Qiu Shen, changed his name to Liu Ni, falsely claimed he was a descendant of Han, and installed him as Son of Heaven, saying: "This is the sage."
translations.idiomatic: He took Qiu Shen, a clerk of Shandu County, changed his name to Liu Ni, and falsely proclaimed him a descendant of the Han. Zhang Chang set him up as emperor, declaring, "This is the sage."

sentences.zh: 昌自為相國，詐作鳳皇、玉璽之瑞，建元神鳳；

translations.literal: Chang made himself Chancellor of State, forged auspicious signs of phoenix and jade seal, and established the era name Yuanfeng;
translations.idiomatic: He made himself chancellor of state, forged omens of phoenixes and a jade seal, and proclaimed the era name Yuanfeng;

sentences.zh: 郊禮、服色，悉依漢故事。

translations.literal: sacrificial rites at the suburbs, regalia and colors—all followed Han precedent.
translations.idiomatic: sacrifices, regalia, and ceremonial colors all followed Han precedent.

sentences.zh: 有不應募者，族誅之，士民莫敢不從。

translations.literal: Those who would not enlist had their clans exterminated; gentry and commoners dared not refuse.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who refused to enlist saw his entire clan put to death. Gentry and commoners alike dared not disobey.

sentences.zh: 又流言：「江、淮已南皆反，官軍大起，當悉誅之。」

translations.literal: He also spread rumors: "South of the Yangzi and Huai all have rebelled; government troops are massing and will execute you all."
translations.idiomatic: He also spread word that "the lands south of the Yangzi and Huai have all risen, and when the government armies march in force, every one of you will be killed."

sentences.zh: 互相扇動，人情惶懼。

translations.literal: They incited one another, and popular sentiment was fearful and alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: People whipped one another into panic, and terror spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 江、沔間所在起兵以應昌，旬月間眾至三萬，皆著絳帽，以馬尾作髯。

translations.literal: Everywhere between the Yangzi and Han troops rose to answer Chang; within a month and ten days the host reached thirty thousand, all wearing crimson caps and using horse tails for beards.
translations.idiomatic: Uprisings answered Zhang Chang all along the Yangzi and Han valleys. Within a month his following reached thirty thousand, each man wearing a crimson cap and a beard made of horsehair.

sentences.zh: 詔遣監軍華宏討之，敗於障山。

translations.literal: An edict dispatched Army Supervisor Hua Hong to campaign against him; he was defeated at Zhang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: The court sent the army supervisor Hua Hong against him, but Hong was defeated at Zhang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 歆上言：「妖賊犬羊萬計，絳頭毛面，挑刀走戟，其鋒不可當。

translations.literal: Xin memorialized upward: "The demonic rebels number tens of thousands like dogs and sheep, with crimson heads and hairy faces, brandishing blades and running with halberds—their momentum cannot be withstood.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xin memorialized the throne: "The sorcerous rebels swarm in their tens of thousands like dogs and sheep, crimson-capped and bearded, blades in hand and halberds at the run—their onset cannot be stopped.

sentences.zh: 請台敕諸軍三道救助。」

translations.literal: I beg the central government to order all armies to aid us on three routes."
translations.idiomatic: I beg the court to order relief armies to advance on three fronts."

sentences.zh: 朝廷以屯騎校尉劉喬為豫州刺史，寧塑將軍沛國劉弘為荊州刺史。

translations.literal: The court appointed Commandant of Garrison Cavalry Liu Qiao as Inspector of Yuzhou and Pacification General Liu Hong of Pei as Inspector of Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The court named Liu Qiao, commandant of garrison cavalry, inspector of Yuzhou, and Liu Hong of Pei, pacification general, inspector of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 又詔河間王顒遣雍州刺史劉沈將州兵萬人，並征西府五千人出藍田頭以討昌。

translations.literal: It further ordered Prince of Hejian Yong to send Yong Province Inspector Liu Shen with ten thousand provincial troops, together with five thousand from the Western Campaign headquarters, out from Lantian Pass to campaign against Chang.
translations.idiomatic: It also ordered Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian, to send Liu Shen, inspector of Yong Province, with ten thousand provincial troops plus five thousand from the western campaign headquarters through Lantian Pass against Zhang Chang.

sentences.zh: 顒不奉詔；

translations.literal: Yong did not obey the edict;
translations.idiomatic: Yong ignored the edict;

sentences.zh: 沈自領州兵至藍田，顒又逼奪其眾。

translations.literal: Shen himself led provincial troops to Lantian, and Yong again coerced away his host.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shen marched his provincial troops to Lantian on his own authority, but Yong seized his army from him by force.

sentences.zh: 於是劉喬屯汝南，劉弘及前將軍趙驤、平南將軍羊伊屯宛。

translations.literal: Thereupon Liu Qiao encamped at Runan, and Liu Hong with Forward General Zhao Xiang and Pacification of the South General Yang Yi encamped at Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Qiao then encamped at Runan, while Liu Hong, the forward general Zhao Xiang, and the pacifier of the south Yang Yi took position at Wan.

sentences.zh: 昌遣其將黃林帥二萬人向豫州，劉喬擊卻之。

translations.literal: Chang sent his general Huang Lin to lead twenty thousand men toward Yuzhou; Liu Qiao struck and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang sent his general Huang Lin with twenty thousand men against Yuzhou, but Liu Qiao beat him back.

sentences.zh: 初，歆與齊王冏善，冏敗，歆懼，自結於大將軍穎。

translations.literal: Earlier, Xin had been on good terms with Prince of Qi Jiong; when Jiong was defeated, Xin was afraid and attached himself to Grand General Ying.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Sima Xin had been allied with Sima Jiong, Prince of Qi. When Jiong fell, Xin grew fearful and threw in his lot with the grand general Sima Ying.

sentences.zh: 及張昌作亂，歆表請討之。

translations.literal: When Zhang Chang made rebellion, Xin memorialized requesting to campaign against him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Chang rebelled, Xin petitioned for permission to campaign against him.

sentences.zh: 時長沙王乂已與穎有隙，疑歆與穎連謀，不聽歆出兵，昌眾日盛。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Changsha Yi already had a rift with Ying and suspected Xin of plotting with Ying; he would not permit Xin to send out troops, and Chang's host grew daily.
translations.idiomatic: By then Sima Yi, Prince of Changsha, was already at odds with Sima Ying and suspected Xin of conspiring with him. He refused to let Xin take the field, and Zhang Chang's following grew day by day.

sentences.zh: 從事中郎孫洵謂歆曰：「公為岳牧，受閫外之托，拜表輒行，有何不可！

translations.literal: Attendant Gentleman Sun Xun said to Xin: "Your Grace is a frontier governor entrusted with authority beyond the passes—what is wrong with memorializing and acting at once!
translations.idiomatic: Sun Xun, an attendant gentleman, told Xin, "You are a frontier governor entrusted with power beyond the passes. What harm is there in memorializing the court and marching at once?

sentences.zh: 而使奸凶滋蔓，禍釁不測，豈籓翰王室、鎮靜方夏之義乎！」

translations.literal: Yet you let treacherous villains spread unchecked and disaster loom without measure—is this the duty of a bulwark of the royal house and a pacifier of the realm!"
translations.idiomatic: To let villains spread unchecked while calamity gathers— is that the duty of one who should shield the throne and pacify the realm?"

sentences.zh: 歆將出兵，王綏曰：「昌等小賊，偏裨自足制之，何必違詔命，親矢石也！」

translations.literal: Xin was about to send out troops when Wang Sui said: "Chang and such petty bandits—a subordinate general is enough to subdue them; why violate the edict and face arrows and stones in person!"
translations.idiomatic: Xin was preparing to march when Wang Sui said, "Zhang Chang is a petty bandit. A subordinate general is enough to handle him. Why defy the edict and expose yourself to battle?"

sentences.zh: 昌至樊城，歆乃出拒之。

translations.literal: When Chang reached Fancheng, Xin then went out to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Chang reached Fancheng, Xin at last went out to meet him.

sentences.zh: 眾潰，為昌所殺。

translations.literal: His host collapsed and he was killed by Chang.
translations.idiomatic: His army broke, and Zhang Chang killed him.

sentences.zh: 詔以劉弘代歆為鎮南將軍，都督荊州諸軍事。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Liu Hong to replace Xin as General Who Pacifies the South and Commander-in-Chief of all Jing Province military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named Liu Hong to replace Xin as general who pacifies the south and commander-in-chief of all military affairs in Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 六月，弘以南蠻長史廬江陶侃為大都護，參軍蒯恆為義軍督護，牙門將皮初為都戰帥，進據襄陽。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, Hong appointed Southern Man Chief Clerk Tao Kan of Lujiang as Grand Protector, Staff Officer Kuai Heng as Protector of the Righteous Army, and Gate Officer Pi Chu as Chief Battle Commander, and advanced to occupy Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Hong appointed Tao Kan of Lujiang, chief clerk for the southern tribes, grand protector; Kuai Heng, a staff officer, protector of the righteous army; and Pi Chu, a gate officer, chief battle commander. He advanced and took Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 張昌並軍圍宛，敗趙驤軍，殺羊伊。

translations.literal: Zhang Chang combined his armies to besiege Wan, defeated Zhao Xiang's army, and killed Yang Yi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang united his forces and besieged Wan, routed Zhao Xiang's army, and killed Yang Yi.

sentences.zh: 劉弘退屯梁。

translations.literal: Liu Hong withdrew to encamp at Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong fell back to encamp at Liang.

sentences.zh: 昌進攻襄陽，不克。

translations.literal: Chang advanced to attack Xiangyang but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang attacked Xiangyang but failed to capture it.

sentences.zh: 李雄攻殺汶山太守陳圖，遂取郫城。

translations.literal: Li Xiong attacked and killed Wenshan Administrator Chen Tu, then took Picheng.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong attacked and killed Chen Tu, administrator of Wenshan, and seized Picheng.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，李流徒屯郫。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, Li Liu moved his encampment to Pi.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, Li Liu shifted his camp to Pi.

sentences.zh: 蜀民皆保險結塢，或南入寧州，或東下荊州。

translations.literal: Shu people all held defensible places and formed stockades, or went south into Ningzhou, or east down to Jingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu all fled to fortified stockades in the hills, or went south into Ning Province, or east into Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 城邑皆空，野無煙火，流虜掠無所得，士眾饑乏。

translations.literal: Cities and towns were all empty; in the wilds there was no smoke or fire; Liu's plundering obtained nothing, and officers and soldiers were hungry and destitute.
translations.idiomatic: Towns stood empty and the countryside was bare of hearth smoke. Li Liu's raids yielded nothing, and his soldiers went hungry.

sentences.zh: 唯涪陵千餘家，依青城山處士范長生；

translations.literal: Only more than a thousand households of Fuling relied on Qingcheng Mountain recluse Fan Changsheng;
translations.idiomatic: Only a thousand-odd households in Fuling still looked to Fan Changsheng, a recluse of Mount Qingcheng;

sentences.zh: 平西參軍涪陵徐輿說羅尚，求為汶山太守，邀結長生，與共討流。

translations.literal: Western Pacification Army Staff Officer Xu Yu of Fuling persuaded Luo Shang, asking to be made Wenshan Administrator, to win over Changsheng and campaign against Liu together.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yu of Fuling, a staff officer on the western pacification staff, urged Luo Shang to appoint him administrator of Wenshan so that he could win over Changsheng and join him in campaigning against Li Liu.

sentences.zh: 尚不許，輿怒，出降於流，流以輿為安西將軍。

translations.literal: Shang did not consent; Yu was angry, went out and surrendered to Liu, and Liu made Yu General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang refused. Enraged, Xu Yu went over to Li Liu, who made him general who pacifies the west.

sentences.zh: 輿說長生，使資給流軍糧，長生從之。

translations.literal: Yu persuaded Changsheng to supply grain to Liu's army, and Changsheng complied.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yu persuaded Changsheng to provision Li Liu's army with grain, and Changsheng agreed.

sentences.zh: 流軍由是復振。

translations.literal: Liu's army thereby revived its strength.
translations.idiomatic: Li Liu's army was thereby restored to strength.

sentences.zh: 初，李含以長沙王乂微弱，必為齊王冏所殺，因欲以為冏罪而討之，遂廢帝，立大將軍穎，以河間王顒為宰相，己得用事。

translations.literal: Earlier, Li Han judged that Prince of Changsha Yi was weak and would surely be killed by Prince of Qi Jiong, and so wished to use that as Jiong's crime and campaign against him, then depose the emperor, install Grand General Ying, and make Prince of Hejian Yong prime minister, so that he himself might hold power.
translations.idiomatic: Previously, Li Han had reckoned that the Prince of Changsha, Sima Yi, was weak and would inevitably be killed by the Prince of Qi, Sima Jiong. He intended to frame Jiong with that offense and raise an army against him, then depose the emperor, set up Grand General Sima Ying, install the Prince of Hejian, Sima Yong, as chief minister—and thus seize power for himself.

sentences.zh: 既而冏為乂所殺，穎、顒猶守籓，不如所謀。

translations.literal: Afterward Jiong was killed by Yi, and Ying and Yong still kept to their fiefs—the plan did not unfold as intended.
translations.idiomatic: But then Jiong was killed by Sima Yi after all, while Ying and Yong remained in their princely domains. The scheme miscarried.

sentences.zh: 穎恃功驕奢，百度弛廢，甚於冏時；

translations.literal: Ying relied on his merit and was arrogant and extravagant; every measure fell into neglect, worse than in Jiong's time;
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying swaggered over his achievements, growing arrogant and prodigal. Government collapsed on every front—even worse than under Sima Jiong;

sentences.zh: 猶嫌乂在內，不得逞其欲，欲去之。

translations.literal: He still resented that Yi was inside the capital and could not indulge his desires, and wished to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: He still resented Sima Yi's presence at court, which blocked his ambitions, and he set out to get rid of him.

sentences.zh: 時皇甫商復為乂參軍，商兄重為秦州刺史。

translations.literal: At this time Huangfu Shang again served as Yi's staff officer, and Shang's elder brother Chong was Governor of Qin Province.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Shang was again on Sima Yi's staff, while Shang's elder brother Huangfu Chong served as governor of Qin Province.

sentences.zh: 含說顒曰：「商為乂所任，重終不為人用，宜早除之。

translations.literal: Han persuaded Yong, saying, "Shang is trusted by Yi; Chong will never serve others in the end—you ought to eliminate them early.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han urged Sima Yong: "Huangfu Shang is in Sima Yi's confidence, and Huangfu Chong will never bow to anyone else. They should be removed at once.

sentences.zh: 可表遷重為內職，因其過長安執之。」

translations.literal: One may memorialize to transfer Chong to a post within the capital, and seize him when he passes through Chang'an."
translations.idiomatic: Memorialize to transfer Chong to a court appointment, then arrest him when he passes through Chang'an."

sentences.zh: 重知之，露檄上尚書，發隴上兵以討含。

translations.literal: Chong learned of it, posted an open letter to the Masters of Writing, and raised troops from Longshang to campaign against Han.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Chong learned of the plot. He issued an open proclamation to the Masters of Writing and raised troops from the Long region to march against Li Han.

sentences.zh: 乂以兵方少息，遣使詔重罷兵，征含為河南尹。

translations.literal: Yi, because the armies had just begun to quiet somewhat, sent envoys with an edict ordering Chong to cease his troops and summoning Han to be Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The fighting had only just subsided. Sima Yi sent envoys ordering Chong to stand down his forces and summoning Li Han to take up the post of intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 含就征而重不奉詔，顒遣金城太守游楷、隴西太守韓稚等合四郡兵攻之。

translations.literal: Han obeyed the summons, but Chong did not receive the edict; Yong sent Jincheng Administrator You Kai, Longxi Administrator Han Zhi, and others to combine troops of four commanderies and attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Han answered the summons, but Huangfu Chong refused the edict. Sima Yong dispatched You Kai, administrator of Jincheng, Han Zhi, administrator of Longxi, and others with soldiers from four commanderies to attack him.

sentences.zh: 顒密使含與侍中馮蓀、中書令卞粹謀殺乂；

translations.literal: Yong secretly sent Han, together with Palace Attendant Feng Sun and Secretariat Director Bian Cui, to plot killing Yi;
translations.idiomatic: In secret, Yong sent Li Han to join Palace Attendant Feng Sun and Secretariat Director Bian Cui in a plot to assassinate Sima Yi;

sentences.zh: 皇甫商以告乂，收含、蓀、粹，殺之。

translations.literal: Huangfu Shang reported this to Yi, who arrested Han, Sun, and Cui and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: Huangfu Shang warned Sima Yi. He had Han, Sun, and Cui seized and executed.

sentences.zh: 驃騎從事琅邪諸葛玫、前司徒長史武邑牽秀皆出奔鄴。

translations.literal: Cavalry General's Staff Officer Zhuge Mei of Langye and former Chief Minister's Chief Clerk Qian Xiu of Wuyi both fled to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuge Mei of Langye, staff officer on the cavalry general's staff, and Qian Xiu of Wuyi, former chief clerk under the chief minister, both fled to Ye.

sentences.zh: 張昌黨石冰寇揚州，敗刺史陳徽，諸郡盡沒；

translations.literal: Shi Bing, a partisan of Zhang Chang, raided Yang Province, defeated Inspector Chen Hui, and all the commanderies fell;
translations.idiomatic: Shi Bing, a follower of Zhang Chang, raided Yang Province, routed Inspector Chen Hui, and overrun every commandery in the region;

sentences.zh: 又攻破江州，別將陳貞等攻武陵、零陵、豫章、武昌、長沙，皆陷之，臨淮人封雲起兵寇徐州以應冰。

translations.literal: He also captured Jiang Province; detached commanders Chen Zhen and others attacked Wuling, Lingling, Yuzhang, Wuchang, and Changsha—all fell; Feng Yun of Linhuai raised troops to raid Xu Province in response to Bing.
translations.idiomatic: They also took Jiang Province. Detached generals such as Chen Zhen overran Wuling, Lingling, Yuzhang, Wuchang, and Changsha. Feng Yun of Linhuai raised an army in Xu Province to join Shi Bing.

sentences.zh: 於是荊、江、揚、豫、徐五州之境，多為昌所據。

translations.literal: Thereupon within the territories of Jing, Jiang, Yang, Yu, and Xu—the five provinces—much was held by Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Large stretches of Jing, Jiang, Yang, Yu, and Xu—five provinces in all—now lay under Zhang Chang's control.

sentences.zh: 昌更置牧守，皆桀盜小人，專以劫掠為務。

translations.literal: Chang replaced the governors and administrators, all of them fierce brigands and petty men who devoted themselves solely to plunder.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Chang installed new governors and prefects—violent bandits and lowborn scoundrels whose only occupation was pillage.

sentences.zh: 劉弘遣陶侃等攻昌於竟陵，劉喬遣其將李楊等向江夏。

translations.literal: Liu Hong sent Tao Kan and others to attack Chang at Jingling; Liu Qiao sent his generals Li Yang and others toward Jiangxia.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong dispatched Tao Kan and others to strike Zhang Chang at Jingling, while Liu Qiao sent his generals Li Yang and others toward Jiangxia.

sentences.zh: 侃等屢與昌戰，大破之，前後斬首數萬級，昌逃於下俊山，其眾悉降。

translations.literal: Kan and others repeatedly fought Chang, routed him thoroughly, cut off tens of thousands of heads before and after; Chang fled to Xiajun Mountain, and his followers all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan's forces clashed with Zhang Chang again and again, crushing him in battle. Tens of thousands were beheaded in all. Zhang Chang fled to Mount Xiajun and his men surrendered en masse.

sentences.zh: 初，陶侃少孤貧，為郡督郵。

translations.literal: Earlier, Tao Kan in youth was orphaned and poor, and served as a commandery postal inspector.
translations.idiomatic: Tao Kan had been orphaned and impoverished in his youth, and served as a commandery postal inspector.

sentences.zh: 長沙太守萬嗣過廬江，見而異之，命其子結友而去。

translations.literal: Changsha Administrator Wan Si passed through Lujiang, saw him and found him extraordinary, and ordered his son to befriend him before departing.
translations.idiomatic: When Wan Si, administrator of Changsha, passed through Lujiang, he was struck by the young man and had his son befriend him before continuing on his way.

sentences.zh: 後察孝廉，至洛陽，豫章國郎中令楊卓薦之於顧榮，侃由是知名。

translations.literal: Later he was nominated as Filial and Incorrupt, reached Luoyang, and Yang Zhuo, Director of Langzhong of the Princedom of Yuzhang, recommended him to Gu Rong—Kan thereby became known.
translations.idiomatic: Later nominated as filial and incorrupt, he went to Luoyang. Yang Zhuo, director of Langzhong in the princedom of Yuzhang, recommended him to Gu Rong, and Tao Kan's reputation was made.

sentences.zh: 既克張昌，劉弘謂侃曰：「吾昔為羊公參軍，謂吾後當居身處，今觀卿，必繼老夫矣。」

translations.literal: After Zhang Chang was conquered, Liu Hong said to Kan, "I once served as staff officer to Duke Yang, and he said I would later occupy his place; now looking at you, you will surely succeed this old man."
translations.idiomatic: After Zhang Chang's defeat, Liu Hong told Tao Kan, "When I served as staff officer to Duke Yang, he told me I would one day hold his office. Now that I look at you, I see you will surely succeed me."

sentences.zh: 弘之退屯於梁也，征南將軍范陽王虓遣前長水校尉張奕領荊州。

translations.literal: When Hong had withdrawn and encamped at Liang, the General Who Conquers the South, Prince of Fanyang Sima Xiao, dispatched former Commandant of the Changshui Zhang Yi to take charge of Jing Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Hong withdrew and encamped at Liang, Sima Xiao, the Prince of Fanyang and general who conquers the south, dispatched Zhang Yi, former commandant of the Changshui Guard, to take over Jing Province.

sentences.zh: 弘至，奕不受代，舉兵拒弘。

translations.literal: When Hong arrived, Yi would not accept the transfer and raised troops to resist Hong.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong arrived, but Zhang Yi refused to hand over the province and took up arms against him.

sentences.zh: 弘討奕，斬之。

translations.literal: Hong campaigned against Yi and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong attacked Zhang Yi and had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 時荊部守宰多缺，弘請補選，詔許之，弘敘功銓德，隨才授任，人皆服其公當。

translations.literal: At the time many prefects and administrators in Jing Province were vacant; Hong requested appointments to fill them, and an edict approved; Hong ranked merit and weighed virtue, assigning posts according to talent—all regarded his fairness.
translations.idiomatic: Many prefectural and commandery posts in Jing Province stood vacant. Liu Hong petitioned to fill them, and the court agreed. He weighed merit and character and matched men to offices according to their abilities. Everyone accepted his fairness.

sentences.zh: 弘表皮初補襄陽太守，朝廷以初雖有功而望淺，更以弘婿前東平太守夏侯陟為襄陽太守。

translations.literal: Hong memorialized to appoint Pi Chu as Xiangyang Administrator; the court held that though Chu had merit, his standing was shallow, and instead appointed Hong's son-in-law, former Dongping Administrator Xiahou Zhi, as Xiangyang Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong recommended Pi Chu for administrator of Xiangyang, but the court, though acknowledging Chu's service, judged his standing too slight and instead appointed his son-in-law Xiahou Zhi, former administrator of Dongping, to the post.

sentences.zh: 弘下教曰：「夫治一國者，宜以一國為心，必若姻親然後可用，則荊州十郡，安得十女婿然後為政哉！」

translations.literal: Hong issued an instruction, saying, "One who governs a state ought to take the whole state to heart; if only in-laws may be used, then for Jing Province's ten commanderies, would one need ten sons-in-law before one could govern!"
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong issued a directive: "A governor must govern with the whole province in mind. If only relatives by marriage may be trusted with office, must Jing Province wait for ten sons-in-law before it can be ruled at all!"

sentences.zh: 乃表：「陟姻親，舊制不得相監；

translations.literal: He then memorialized: "Zhi is a relative by marriage; under old regulations one may not supervise one's own kin;
translations.idiomatic: He then submitted a memorial: "Xiahou Zhi is my son-in-law. By ancient statute, a man may not supervise his own kin;

sentences.zh: 皮初之勳，宜見酬報。」

translations.literal: Chu's merit ought to receive reward and recompense."
translations.idiomatic: Pi Chu's achievements deserve proper recognition and reward."

sentences.zh: 詔聽之。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted his request.

sentences.zh: 弘於是勸課農桑，寬刑省賦，公私給足，百姓愛悅。

translations.literal: Hong thereupon urged agriculture and sericulture, eased punishments and reduced levies; public and private supplies were sufficient, and the people loved and rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hong then promoted farming and sericulture, eased punishments, and lightened taxes. Public and private stores filled up, and the people came to love him.

sentences.zh: 河間王顒聞李含等死，即起兵討長沙王乂。

translations.literal: Prince of Hejian Yong, hearing that Li Han and the others were dead, immediately raised troops to campaign against Prince of Changsha Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Yong, Prince of Hejian, learned that Li Han and his accomplices were dead, he immediately raised an army against Sima Yi, the Prince of Changsha.

sentences.zh: 大將軍穎上表請討張昌，許之；

translations.literal: Grand General Ying submitted a memorial requesting to campaign against Zhang Chang, and approval was granted;
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Sima Ying petitioned to lead a campaign against Zhang Chang, and permission was granted;

sentences.zh: 聞昌已平，因欲與顒共攻乂。

translations.literal: Hearing that Chang was already pacified, he then wished to join Yong in attacking Yi.
translations.idiomatic: When he learned that Zhang Chang had already been suppressed, he turned to join Sima Yong in an attack on Sima Yi.

sentences.zh: 盧志諫曰：「公前有大功而委權辭寵，時望美矣。

translations.literal: Lu Zhi remonstrated, saying, "Your Excellency before had great merit yet ceded power and declined favor—your repute was splendid.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi advised him: "Your Grace once achieved great deeds, then relinquished power and declined honors. Your reputation was at its height.

sentences.zh: 今宜頓軍關外，文服入朝，此霸主之事也。」

translations.literal: Now you ought to halt your army outside the passes, enter court in civil robes—this is the conduct of a hegemon."
translations.idiomatic: Now you ought to halt your army outside the passes and enter the capital in court dress. That is how a true overlord behaves."

sentences.zh: 參軍魏郡邵續曰：「人之有兄弟，如左右手。

translations.literal: Staff Officer Shao Xu of Wei Commandery said, "A man's having brothers is like having left and right hands.
translations.idiomatic: Shao Xu of Wei Commandery, a member of his staff, said, "Brothers are to a man what his two hands are.

sentences.zh: 明公欲當天下之敵而先去其一手，可乎！」

translations.literal: Your Excellency wishes to face the empire's enemies yet first cut off one hand—can this be done!"
translations.idiomatic: Your Grace means to take on the enemies of the realm, yet would cut off one hand first—how can that be right?"

sentences.zh: 穎皆不從。

translations.literal: Ying heeded neither.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying ignored them both.

sentences.zh: 八月，顒、穎共表：「乂論功不平，與右僕射羊玄之、左將軍皇甫商專擅朝政，殺害忠良，請誅玄之、商，遣乂還國。」

translations.literal: In the eighth month, Yong and Ying jointly submitted a memorial: "Yi awards merit unfairly; together with Right Vice Director Yang Xuanshi and Left General Huangfu Shang he monopolizes court governance, kills loyal and worthy men—we request execution of Xuanshi and Shang, and that Yi be sent back to his princedom."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, Yong and Ying jointly petitioned: "Sima Yi distributes rewards unfairly. Together with Yang Xuanshi, right vice director, and Huangfu Shang, left general, he has seized control of the court and murdered loyal ministers. We ask that Xuanshi and Shang be executed and that Sima Yi be sent back to his princedom."

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「顒敢舉大兵，內向京輦，吾當親帥六軍以誅奸逆。

translations.literal: An edict said, "Yong dares raise a great army and turn inward on the capital—I shall personally lead the Six Armies to execute traitors and rebels.
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied: "Yong dares march a great army against the capital. I shall personally lead the Six Armies to destroy these traitors.

sentences.zh: 其以乂為太尉，都督中外諸軍事以御之。」

translations.literal: Let Yi be made Grand Commandant, Grand Commander of All Armies Within and Without, to oppose them."
translations.idiomatic: Let Sima Yi be appointed grand commandant and grand commander of all armies within and without to meet this threat."

sentences.zh: 顒以張方為都督，將精兵七萬，自函谷東趨洛陽。

translations.literal: Yong made Zhang Fang commander-in-chief, leading seventy thousand crack troops from Hangu Pass eastward toward Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yong put Zhang Fang in supreme command and sent seventy thousand elite troops east from Hangu Pass toward Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 穎引兵屯朝歌，以平原內史陸機為前將軍、前鋒都督、督北中郎將王粹、冠軍將軍牽秀、中護軍石超等軍二十餘萬，南向洛陽。

translations.literal: Ying led troops to encamp at Chaoge, appointing Plain Interior Grand Administrator Lu Ji as Forward General, vanguard commander-in-chief, commanding North Corps General Wang Cui, Champion General Qian Xiu, Central Guard General Shi Chao, and others—more than two hundred thousand troops—south toward Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying encamped at Chaoge. He made Lu Ji, interior grand administrator of Pingyuan, forward general and supreme commander of the vanguard, with more than two hundred thousand men under him—including Wang Cui, north corps general; Qian Xiu, champion general; Shi Chao, central guard general—and marched south on Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 機以羈旅事穎，一旦頓居諸將之右，王粹等心皆不服。

translations.literal: Ji, a stranger in service to Ying, suddenly being placed to the right of all the generals—Wang Cui and the others were all resentful in heart.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji was an outsider in Sima Ying's service, yet overnight he stood above veteran generals. Wang Cui and the rest seethed with resentment.

sentences.zh: 白沙督孫惠與機親厚，勸機讓都督於粹。

translations.literal: Baisha Supervisor Sun Hui was on intimate terms with Ji and urged Ji to yield the command to Cui.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Hui, supervisor at Baisha, was close to Lu Ji and urged him to yield command to Wang Cui.

sentences.zh: 機曰：「彼將謂吾首鼠兩端，適所以速禍也。」

translations.literal: Ji said, "They will say I am wavering between two sides—this would only hasten disaster."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji replied, "They would take that for vacillation, and that would only bring ruin faster."

sentences.zh: 遂行。

translations.literal: He then set out.
translations.idiomatic: He marched on all the same.

sentences.zh: 穎列軍自朝歌至河橋，鼓聲聞數百里。

translations.literal: Ying arrayed his army from Chaoge to He Bridge; the drum rolls were heard for several hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying drew up his lines from Chaoge to He Bridge; the thunder of war drums carried for hundreds of li.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，帝如十三里橋。

translations.literal: On yichou, the emperor went to Shisanli Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: On the day yichou, the emperor went to Shisanli Bridge.

sentences.zh: 太尉乂使皇甫商將萬餘人拒張方於宜陽。

translations.literal: Grand Commandant Yi sent Huangfu Shang with more than ten thousand men to oppose Zhang Fang at Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Commandant Sima Yi sent Huangfu Shang with more than ten thousand men to block Zhang Fang at Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 己已，帝還軍宣武場，庚午，捨於石樓。

translations.literal: On jisi, the emperor returned his army to the Military Review Ground; on gengwu, he lodged at Shilou.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, the emperor withdrew his forces to the Military Review Ground; on gengwu, he halted at Shilou.

sentences.zh: 九月，丁丑，屯於河橋。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on dingchou, he encamped at He Bridge.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on dingchou, he encamped at He Bridge.

sentences.zh: 壬子，張方襲皇甫商，敗之。

translations.literal: On renzi, Zhang Fang raided Huangfu Shang and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi, Zhang Fang launched a surprise attack on Huangfu Shang and routed him.

sentences.zh: 甲申，帝軍於芒山。

translations.literal: On jiashen, the emperor encamped his army at Mang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, the emperor posted his army on Mang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，帝幸偃師；

translations.literal: On dinghai, the emperor went to Yanshi;
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, the emperor went to Yanshi;

sentences.zh: 辛卯，捨於豆田。

translations.literal: On xinmao, he lodged at Doutian.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao, he halted at Doutian.

sentences.zh: 大將軍穎進屯河南，阻清水為壘。

translations.literal: Grand General Ying advanced to encamp at Henan, blocking the Qingshui River to make ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Sima Ying pressed forward and encamped in Henan, damming the Qingshui River to build fortifications.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，羊玄之憂懼而卒，帝旋軍城東；

translations.literal: On guisi, Yang Xuanshi died from worry and fear; the emperor wheeled his army to the east of the city;
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Yang Xuanshi died of anxiety and fear. The emperor turned his army back toward the east of the city;

sentences.zh: 丙申，幸緱氏，擊牽秀，走之。

translations.literal: On bingshen, he went to Gou; attacked Qian Xiu and drove him off.
translations.idiomatic: On bingshen, he went to Gou, attacked Qian Xiu, and put him to flight.

sentences.zh: 大赦。

translations.literal: A general amnesty was proclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: A general amnesty was proclaimed.

sentences.zh: 張方入京城，大掠，死者萬計。

translations.literal: Zhang Fang entered the capital city, plundered on a great scale; the dead numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Fang entered the capital and plundered without restraint. Tens of thousands perished.

sentences.zh: 李流疾篤，謂諸將曰：「驍騎仁明，固足以濟大事；

translations.literal: Li Liu was gravely ill and said to the generals, "The Flying Cavalry is humane and bright—he is indeed sufficient to accomplish the great task;
translations.idiomatic: Li Liu lay gravely ill. He told his commanders, "The Flying Cavalry is wise and humane—he can certainly carry the great enterprise through;

sentences.zh: 然前軍英武，殆天所相，可共受事於前軍。」

translations.literal: Yet the Forward Army is heroic and martial—perhaps Heaven's chosen; you may all entrust affairs to the Forward Army."
translations.idiomatic: But the forward army is bold and able—perhaps heaven's chosen. Let all of you take your orders from him."

sentences.zh: 流卒，眾推李雄為大都督、大將軍、益州牧、治郫城。

translations.literal: When Liu died, the multitude acclaimed Li Xiong as Grand Commander-in-Chief, Grand General, Governor of Yi Province, with government at Pixi City.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Liu died, the troops acclaimed Li Xiong as grand commander-in-chief, grand general, and governor of Yi Province, with his seat at Pixi.

sentences.zh: 雄使武都樸泰紿羅尚，使襲郫城，雲己為內應。

translations.literal: Xiong sent Pu Tai of Wudu to deceive Luo Shang, inducing him to attack Pixi, claiming that Tai himself would serve as inside collaborator.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiong sent Pu Tai of Wudu to trick Luo Shang into sending troops against Pixi, claiming that Tai would serve as their inside contact.

sentences.zh: 尚使隗伯將兵攻郫，泰約舉火為應，李驤伏兵於道，泰出長梯於外。

translations.literal: Shang sent Wei Bo to lead troops to attack Pi; Tai agreed to raise fire as signal; Li Xiang lay in ambush on the road; Tai put out long ladders outside.
translations.idiomatic: Luo Shang sent Wei Bo to attack Pixi. Tai promised to signal with torches. Li Xiang hid troops along the road, while Tai rigged long scaling ladders outside the walls.

sentences.zh: 隗伯兵見火起，爭緣梯上，驤縱兵擊，大破之。

translations.literal: When Wei's soldiers saw the fire rise, they scrambled up the ladders; Xiang unleashed his troops and struck, routing them thoroughly.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei Bo's men saw the flames, they rushed up the ladders. Li Xiang's ambush sprang and shattered them.

sentences.zh: 追奔夜至城下，詐稱萬歲，曰：「已得郫城矣！」

translations.literal: Pursuing the fugitives by night to the foot of the city, they falsely shouted "Long live!" saying, "Pixi is already taken!"
translations.idiomatic: They pursued the fugitives through the night to the city walls, shouting false cheers: "Pixi is ours!"

sentences.zh: 入少城，尚乃覺之，退保太城。

translations.literal: They entered Shaocheng; only then did Shang realize it, and retreated to hold Taicheng.
translations.idiomatic: They burst into Shaocheng before Luo Shang understood what was happening. He withdrew to hold Taicheng.

sentences.zh: 隗伯創甚，雄生獲之，赦不殺。

translations.literal: Wei Bo was gravely wounded; Xiong captured him alive and pardoned him without killing.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Bo was badly wounded. Li Xiong took him alive and spared his life.

sentences.zh: 李驤攻犍為，斷尚運道。

translations.literal: Li Xiang attacked Jianwei and cut Shang's supply route.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiang attacked Jianwei and severed Luo Shang's supply lines.

sentences.zh: 獲太守龔恢，殺之。

translations.literal: He captured Administrator Gong Hui and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: He captured Prefect Gong Hui and executed him.

sentences.zh: 石超進逼緱氏。

translations.literal: Shi Chao pressed forward toward Gou.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Chao pressed his advance on Gou.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，壬寅，帝還宮。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on renyin, the emperor returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on renyin, the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 丁未，敗牽秀於東陽門外。

translations.literal: On dingwei, Qian Xiu was defeated outside the Dongyang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Qian Xiu was defeated outside the Dongyang Gate.

sentences.zh: 大將軍穎遣將軍馬咸助陸機。

translations.literal: Grand General Ying dispatched General Ma Xian to assist Lu Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Sima Ying sent General Ma Xian to reinforce Lu Ji.

sentences.zh: 戊申，太尉乂奉帝與機戰於建春門。

translations.literal: On wushen, Grand Commandant Yi escorted the emperor and fought Ji at the Jianchun Gate.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Grand Commandant Sima Yi accompanied the emperor and fought Lu Ji at the Jianchun Gate.

sentences.zh: 乂司馬王瑚使數千騎繫戟於馬，以突咸陳，咸軍亂，執而斬之。

translations.literal: Yi's Major-General Wang Hu sent several thousand cavalry with halberds tied to their horses to burst into Xian's formation; Xian's army fell into disorder, and he was seized and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi's major-general Wang Hu sent several thousand horsemen with halberds lashed to their saddles to crash into Ma Xian's line. Ma Xian's troops collapsed; he was seized and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 機軍大敗，赴七里澗，死者如積，水為之不流。

translations.literal: Ji's army was utterly defeated; they fled into the Qili Stream—corpses piled up like hills, and the water would not flow.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji's army was smashed. Survivors plunged into the Qili Stream; the dead piled so deep the water ceased to flow.

sentences.zh: 斬其大將賈崇等十六人，石超遁去。

translations.literal: Sixteen of his great generals including Jia Chong were beheaded; Shi Chao fled.
translations.idiomatic: Sixteen of his senior commanders, including Jia Chong, were beheaded. Shi Chao escaped.

sentences.zh: 初，宦人孟玖有寵於大將軍穎，玖欲用其父為邯鄲令，左長史盧志等皆不敢違，右司馬陸雲固執不許，曰：「此縣，公府掾資，豈有黃門父居之邪！」

translations.literal: Earlier, the eunuch Meng Jiu had favor with Grand General Ying; Jiu wished to install his father as Handan Magistrate; Left Chief Clerk Lu Zhi and others all dared not disobey, but Right Major-General Lu Yun firmly refused, saying, "This county is a qualification post for the princely staff—how can a eunuch's father hold it!"
translations.idiomatic: The eunuch Meng Jiu had won Grand General Sima Ying's favor. Jiu wanted his father appointed magistrate of Handan. Left chief clerk Lu Zhi and the rest did not dare refuse, but right major-general Lu Yun stood firm against it: "That county is a stepping-stone for the prince's staff. How can a eunuch's father occupy it!"

sentences.zh: 玖深怨之。

translations.literal: Jiu deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Jiu nursed a deep grudge against him.

sentences.zh: 玖弟超，領萬人為小督，未戰，縱兵大掠，陸機錄其主者；

translations.literal: Jiu's younger brother Chao commanded ten thousand men as a minor commander; before battle he let his troops plunder on a great scale; Lu Ji registered the ringleaders;
translations.idiomatic: Jiu's younger brother Chao commanded ten thousand men as a junior commander. Before battle even began, his troops looted freely. Lu Ji had the ringleaders recorded for punishment;

sentences.zh: 超將鐵騎百餘人直入機麾下，奪之，顧謂機曰：「貉奴，能作督不！」

translations.literal: Chao led more than a hundred armored cavalry straight into Ji's headquarters, snatched them back, turned and said to Ji, "Raccoon-dog slave—can you be a commander or not!"
translations.idiomatic: Chao rode in with more than a hundred armored horsemen, burst into Lu Ji's headquarters, and seized the prisoners back. He turned on Lu Ji and said, "You filthy barbarian—do you think you can command!"

sentences.zh: 機司馬吳郡孫拯勸機殺之，機不能用。

translations.literal: Ji's Major-General Sun Zheng of Wu Commandery urged Ji to kill him; Ji could not bring himself to do it.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Ji's major-general Sun Zheng of Wu Commandery urged him to kill Chao. Lu Ji could not bring himself to do it.

sentences.zh: 超宣言於眾曰：「陸機將反。」

translations.literal: Chao proclaimed to the multitude: "Lu Ji is about to rebel."
translations.idiomatic: Chao declared to the troops that Lu Ji was about to rebel."

sentences.zh: 又還書與玖，言機持兩端，故軍不速決。

translations.literal: He also sent a letter back to Jiu, saying Ji was wavering between two sides, and therefore the army did not achieve a quick decision.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Meng Jiu, claiming Lu Ji was hedging and that was why the army had not won quickly.

sentences.zh: 及戰，超不受機節度，輕兵獨進，敗沒。

translations.literal: When battle came, Chao did not accept Ji's command; with light troops he advanced alone and was defeated and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: When the fighting began, Chao ignored Lu Ji's orders, led a light detachment forward on his own, and was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 玖疑機殺之，譖之於穎曰：「機有二心於長沙。」

translations.literal: Jiu suspected Ji had killed him and slandered Ji to Ying, saying, "Ji has divided loyalties toward Prince of Changsha."
translations.idiomatic: Meng Jiu suspected Lu Ji of having killed his brother and slandered him to Sima Ying, saying Lu Ji was secretly loyal to the Prince of Changsha."

sentences.zh: 牽秀素謅事玖，將軍王闡、郝昌、帳下督陽平公師籓皆玖所引用，相與共證之。

translations.literal: Qian Xiu had always flattered Jiu; Generals Wang Chan, Hao Chang, and Staff Supervisor Yangping Duke Shi Fan were all appointed by Jiu—they corroborated together.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Xiu had always fawned on Meng Jiu. Generals Wang Chan and Hao Chang, and staff supervisor the Duke of Yangping, Shi Fan—all Jiu's appointees—joined in testifying against Lu Ji.

sentences.zh: 穎大怒，使秀將兵收機。

translations.literal: Ying was greatly enraged and ordered Xiu to lead troops to seize Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying flew into a rage and ordered Qian Xiu to take troops and arrest Lu Ji.

sentences.zh: 參軍事王彰諫曰：「今日之舉，強弱異勢。

translations.literal: Staff Member Wang Zhang remonstrated, saying, "In today's campaign, strength and weakness are mismatched.
translations.idiomatic: Staff officer Wang Zhang urged caution: "In this campaign, the balance of force does not favor us.

sentences.zh: 庸人猶知必克，況機之明達乎！

translations.literal: Even a dull man would know victory is certain—how much more so one as clear-sighted as Ji!
translations.idiomatic: Even a fool can see we are sure to win—how much more so a man as brilliant as Lu Ji!

sentences.zh: 但機吳人，殿下用之太過，北土舊將皆疾之耳。」

translations.literal: Only, Ji is a man of Wu; Your Highness has used him too greatly—the old generals of the north all resent him, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: It is simply that Lu Ji is a southerner. Your Highness has elevated him too far, and the northern veterans resent it—that is all."

sentences.zh: 穎不從。

translations.literal: Ying did not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying would not hear it.

sentences.zh: 機聞秀至，釋戎服，著白帢，與秀相見，為箋辭穎，既而歎曰：「華亭鶴唳，可復聞呼！」

translations.literal: When Ji heard Xiu had arrived, he removed his military garb, put on a white headcloth, met with Xiu, and wrote a memorial of farewell to Ying; then he sighed and said, "The cranes calling at Huating—shall I ever hear them again!"
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Ji learned that Qian Xiu had arrived, he laid aside his armor, put on a plain white cap, and went to meet him. He wrote a farewell memorial to Sima Ying, then sighed: "The cranes of Huating—will I ever hear them call again?"

sentences.zh: 秀遂殺之。

translations.literal: Xiu then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Xiu then executed him.

sentences.zh: 穎又收機弟清河內史雲、平東祭酒耽及孫拯，皆下獄。

translations.literal: Ying also arrested Ji's younger brother Yun, Interior Minister of Qinghe, Pingdong Libationer Dan, and Sun Zheng—all were thrown into prison.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying also arrested Lu Ji's younger brother Lu Yun, interior minister of Qinghe, the Pingdong libationer Dan, and Sun Zheng—all were thrown into prison.

sentences.zh: 記室江統、陳留蔡克、穎川棗嵩等上疏，以為：「陸機淺謀致敗，殺之可也。

translations.literal: Registrar Jiang Tong, Cai Ke of Chenliu, Zao Song of Yingchuan, and others submitted a memorial, arguing: "Lu Ji's shallow strategy led to defeat; executing him would be acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: The registrar Jiang Tong, Cai Ke of Chenliu, Zao Song of Yingchuan, and others submitted a memorial arguing that Lu Ji's shallow strategy had brought defeat and that his execution would be justified.

sentences.zh: 至於反逆，則眾共知其不然。

translations.literal: As for rebellion, everyone together knows that is not so.
translations.idiomatic: As for treason, everyone knew that was not true.

sentences.zh: 宜先檢校機反狀，若有徵驗，誅雲等未晚也。」

translations.literal: It would be proper first to investigate evidence of Ji's rebellion; if proof is found, executing Yun and the others would not be too late."
translations.idiomatic: They should first examine the evidence of Lu Ji's rebellion; if proof were found, executing Lu Yun and the others would not be too late."

sentences.zh: 統等懇請不已，穎遲回者三日。

translations.literal: Jiang Tong and the others pleaded incessantly; Ying wavered for three days.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Tong and the others pleaded without cease, and Sima Ying hesitated for three days.

sentences.zh: 蔡克入，至穎前，叩頭流血，曰：「雲為孟玖所犯，遠近莫不聞。

translations.literal: Cai Ke entered, came before Ying, knocked his head until it bled, and said, "Yun was wronged by Meng Jiu—near and far, who has not heard of it?
translations.idiomatic: Cai Ke went in, came before Sima Ying, and knocked his head on the ground until it bled. He said, "Lu Yun was wronged by Meng Jiu—everyone near and far has heard of it.

sentences.zh: 今果見殺，竊為明公惜之！」

translations.literal: If he is indeed killed now, I privately grieve for Your Excellency!"
translations.idiomatic: If he is killed after all, I shall grieve for Your Excellency's sake!"

sentences.zh: 僚屬隨克入者數十人，流涕固請，穎惻然，有宥雲之色。

translations.literal: Several dozen retainers who followed Ke in wept and pressed their plea; Ying looked pained and seemed inclined to spare Yun.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen staff members who had followed Cai Ke in wept and pleaded insistently. Sima Ying was moved and seemed ready to spare Lu Yun.

sentences.zh: 孟玖扶穎入，催令殺雲、耽，夷機三族。

translations.literal: Meng Jiu supported Ying inside and urged that Yun and Dan be killed and the three clans related to Ji be exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Jiu helped Sima Ying inside and pressed him to have Lu Yun and Dan executed and to exterminate the three clans of the Lu family.

sentences.zh: 獄吏考掠孫拯數百，兩踝骨見，終言機冤。

translations.literal: Prison officials tortured Sun Zheng hundreds of times until the bones of both ankles were exposed; to the end he maintained that Ji had been wronged.
translations.idiomatic: Prison officials tortured Sun Zheng hundreds of times until the bones of both his ankles showed through, yet to the end he maintained that Lu Ji had been wronged.

sentences.zh: 吏知拯義烈，謂拯曰：「二陸之枉，誰不知之，君可不愛身乎！」

translations.literal: The officials knew Zheng was righteous and resolute and said to him, "The injustice done to the two Lus—who does not know it? Sir, can you not value your own life!"
translations.idiomatic: The officials knew Sun Zheng was a man of integrity and said to him, "The injustice done to the two Lus—who does not know it? Why not spare your own life!"

sentences.zh: 拯仰天歎曰：「陸君兄弟，世之奇士，吾蒙知愛，今既不能救其死，忍復從而誣之乎！」

translations.literal: Zheng sighed heavenward and said, "The Lu brothers were extraordinary men of their age; I received their kindness and trust. Now that I cannot save them from death, how can I bear to join in slandering them!"
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zheng looked up to heaven and sighed, "The Lu brothers were extraordinary men of their age. I received their kindness and trust. Now that I cannot save them from death, how can I bear to join in slandering them!"

sentences.zh: 玖等知拯不可屈，乃令獄吏詐為拯辭。

translations.literal: When Jiu and the others saw that Zheng could not be broken, they had prison officials forge a confession in his name.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Jiu and the others saw that Sun Zheng could not be broken, they had prison officials forge a confession in his name.

sentences.zh: 穎既殺機，意常悔之，及見拯辭，大喜，謂玖等曰：「非卿之忠，不能窮此奸。」

translations.literal: Ying, having already killed Ji, often regretted it; when he saw Zheng's confession he was greatly pleased and said to Jiu and the others, "Were it not for your loyalty, this treachery could not have been fully exposed."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying, having already killed Lu Ji, often regretted it. When he saw Sun Zheng's confession he was greatly pleased and said to Meng Jiu and the others, "Were it not for your loyalty, this conspiracy could never have been fully exposed."

sentences.zh: 遂夷拯三族。

translations.literal: He then exterminated the three clans of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: He then exterminated the three clans of Sun Zheng.

sentences.zh: 拯門人費慈、宰意二人詣獄明拯冤，拯譬遣之曰：「吾義不負二陸，死自吾分；

translations.literal: Zheng's students Fei Ci and Zai Yi, two men, went to the prison to declare Zheng's innocence; Zheng sent them away with a parable, saying, "In righteousness I will not fail the two Lus; death is my allotted portion;
translations.idiomatic: Sun Zheng's students Fei Ci and Zai Yi went to the prison to declare his innocence. Sun Zheng sent them away with a rebuke: "In righteousness I will not fail the two Lus. Death is my allotted portion;

sentences.zh: 卿何為爾邪！」

translations.literal: why do you act like this!"
translations.idiomatic: why are you doing this!"

sentences.zh: 曰：「君既不負二陸，僕又安可負君！」

translations.literal: They said, "Since you will not fail the two Lus, how could I fail you!"
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "Since you will not fail the two Lus, how could I fail you!"

sentences.zh: 固言拯冤，玖又殺之。

translations.literal: They persisted in declaring Zheng's innocence; Jiu had them killed as well.
translations.idiomatic: They persisted in declaring Sun Zheng's innocence, and Meng Jiu had them killed as well.

sentences.zh: 太尉乂奉帝攻張方，方兵望見乘輿，皆退走，方遂大敗，死才五千餘人。

translations.literal: Grand Marshal Yi escorted the emperor to attack Zhang Fang; when Fang's troops saw the imperial carriage they all retreated and fled; Fang suffered a great defeat, though only a little more than five thousand died.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Sima Yi escorted the emperor to attack Zhang Fang. When Fang's troops saw the imperial carriage they all fell back and fled. Fang suffered a crushing defeat, though only a little more than five thousand men were killed.

sentences.zh: 方退屯十三里橋，眾懼，欲夜遁，方曰：「勝負兵家之常，善用兵者能因敗為成。

translations.literal: Fang withdrew and encamped at Shisanli Bridge; the troops were afraid and wanted to flee by night. Fang said, "Victory and defeat are the constant of warfare; one who knows how to use troops can turn defeat into triumph.
translations.idiomatic: Fang withdrew and encamped at Shisanli Bridge. His troops were terrified and wanted to flee by night. Fang said, "Victory and defeat are the common lot of war. A commander who knows his craft can turn defeat into triumph.

sentences.zh: 今我更前作壘，出其不意，此奇策也。」

translations.literal: Now if I advance again and build fortifications, catching them unawares—this is a bold stratagem."
translations.idiomatic: If I advance again now and build fortifications, catching them unawares—that is a bold stratagem."

sentences.zh: 乃夜潛進，逼洛城七里，築壘數重，外引廩谷以足軍食。

translations.literal: That night he advanced secretly, approaching within seven li of Luoyang, built several rings of fortifications, and drew grain from outside granaries to supply the army's food.
translations.idiomatic: That night he advanced in secret, coming within seven li of Luoyang. He built several rings of fortifications and drew grain from outside granaries to feed his army.

sentences.zh: 乂既戰勝，以為方不足憂。

translations.literal: Yi, having won the battle, thought Fang was not worth worrying about.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi, having won the battle, thought Zhang Fang was no longer worth worrying about.

sentences.zh: 聞方壘成，十一月，引兵攻之，不利。

translations.literal: When he heard Fang's fortifications were complete, in the eleventh month he led troops to attack them—without success.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Fang's fortifications were complete, in the eleventh month he led troops to attack them—but without success.

sentences.zh: 朝議以乂、穎兄弟，可辭說而釋，乃使中書令王衍等往說穎，令與乂分陝而居，穎不從。

translations.literal: Court deliberations held that Yi and Ying, being brothers, could be persuaded to reconcile; they therefore sent Palace Secretary Wang Yan and others to persuade Ying to divide the realm at Shan and live apart from Yi—Ying refused.
translations.idiomatic: Court deliberations held that Sima Yi and Sima Ying, being brothers, could be persuaded to reconcile. They sent Palace Secretary Wang Yan and others to urge Ying to divide the realm at Mount Shan and govern apart from Yi—but Ying refused.

sentences.zh: 乂因致書於穎，為陳利害，欲與之和解，穎復書：「請斬皇甫商等首，則引兵還鄴。」

translations.literal: Yi then sent a letter to Ying setting forth advantages and disadvantages, wishing to make peace with him. Ying replied, "Cut off the heads of Huangfu Shang and the others, and I will withdraw my troops to Ye."
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi then wrote to Sima Ying, setting forth the advantages and disadvantages of war and seeking reconciliation. Ying replied, "Cut off the heads of Huangfu Shang and the others, and I will withdraw my troops to Ye."

sentences.zh: 乂不可。

translations.literal: Yi would not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi would not agree.

sentences.zh: 穎進兵逼京師，張方決千金堨，水碓皆涸。

translations.literal: Ying advanced and pressed upon the capital; Zhang Fang breached the Qianjin Dyke, and all the water mills ran dry.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Ying advanced and pressed upon the capital. Zhang Fang breached the Qianjin Dyke, and all the water mills ran dry.

sentences.zh: 乃發王公奴婢手舂給兵，一品已下不從征者，男子十三以上皆從役，又發奴助兵；

translations.literal: They then conscripted the palace servants and slaves of nobles and officials to pound grain by hand for the troops; all men of rank one and below not on campaign, thirteen years and older, were put to service; slaves were also mobilized to assist the army;
translations.idiomatic: They conscripted the palace servants and slaves of nobles and officials to pound grain by hand for the troops. All men of rank one and below who were not on campaign, thirteen years and older, were put to service, and slaves were also mobilized to assist the army;

sentences.zh: 公私窮踧，米石萬錢。

translations.literal: Public and private resources were exhausted; a shi of rice cost ten thousand cash.
translations.idiomatic: Public and private resources were exhausted. A shi of rice cost ten thousand cash.

sentences.zh: 詔命所行，一城而已。

translations.literal: Imperial edicts reached no farther than the one city.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial edicts reached no farther than the one city.

sentences.zh: 驃騎主簿范陽祖逖言於乂曰：「劉沈忠義果毅，雍州兵力足制河間，宜啟上為詔與沈，使發兵襲顒。

translations.literal: Rapid Cavalry Chief Clerk Zu Ti of Fanyang said to Yi, "Liu Shen is loyal, righteous, and resolute; Yong Province's military strength is sufficient to control Hejian. Your Highness should petition the throne for an edict to Shen, directing him to raise troops and strike Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Ti of Fanyang, chief clerk to the Rapid Cavalry General, said to Sima Yi, "Liu Shen is loyal, resolute, and bold. Yong Province's military strength is sufficient to control the Prince of Hejian. Your Highness should petition the throne for an edict to Shen, directing him to raise troops and strike Sima Yong.

sentences.zh: 顒窘急，必召張方以自救，此良策也。」

translations.literal: When Yong is hard pressed he is sure to summon Zhang Fang to save himself—this is an excellent strategy."
translations.idiomatic: When Yong is hard pressed he is sure to summon Zhang Fang to save himself. That is an excellent strategy."

sentences.zh: 乂從之。

translations.literal: Yi followed this advice.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi followed this advice.

sentences.zh: 沈奉詔馳檄四境，諸郡多起兵應之。

translations.literal: Shen received the edict and dispatched proclamations in haste to the four borders; many commanderies raised troops in response.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shen received the edict and dispatched proclamations in haste to the four borders. Many commanderies raised troops in response.

sentences.zh: 沈合七郡之眾凡萬餘人，趣長安。

translations.literal: Shen assembled the forces of seven commanderies, more than ten thousand in all, and marched toward Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shen assembled the forces of seven commanderies, more than ten thousand in all, and marched toward Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 乂又使皇甫商間行，繼帝手詔，命游楷等罷兵，敕皇甫重進軍討顒。

translations.literal: Yi also sent Huangfu Shang by secret route, carrying the emperor's handwritten edict in succession, ordering You Kai and the others to stand down their armies and commanding Huangfu Chong to advance and attack Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yi also sent Huangfu Shang by secret route, bearing the emperor's handwritten edict in succession, ordering You Kai and the others to stand down their armies and commanding Huangfu Chong to advance and attack Sima Yong.

sentences.zh: 商間行至新平，遇其從甥，從甥素憎商，以告顒捕商，殺之。

translations.literal: Shang traveled secretly as far as Xinping, where he met his nephew by marriage; the nephew had always hated Shang and informed on him; Yong captured Shang and killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Shang traveled secretly as far as Xinping, where he met his nephew by marriage. The nephew had always hated Shang and informed on him. Sima Yong captured Shang and killed him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，議郎周玘、前南平內史長沙王矩起兵江東以討石冰，推前吳興太守吳郡顧秘都督揚州九郡諸軍事，傳檄州郡，殺冰所署將吏。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Consultant Gentleman Zhou Qi and former Interior Minister of Nanping Wang Ju of Changsha raised troops in Jiangdong to attack Shi Bing; they recommended former Administrator of Wuxing Gu Mi of Wu Commandery as Commander-in-Chief of Military Affairs for the Nine Commanderies of Yang Province, circulated proclamations through the provinces and commanderies, and killed the generals and officials Bing had appointed.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, consultant gentleman Zhou Qi and former interior minister of Nanping Wang Ju of Changsha raised troops in Jiangdong to attack Shi Bing. They recommended former administrator of Wuxing Gu Mi of Wu Commandery as commander-in-chief of military affairs for the nine commanderies of Yang Province, circulated proclamations through the provinces and commanderies, and killed the generals and officials Shi Bing had appointed.

sentences.zh: 於是前侍御史賀循起兵於會稽，廬江內史廣陵華譚及丹揚葛洪、甘卓皆起兵以應秘。

translations.literal: Thereupon former Attendant Censor He Xun raised troops at Kuaiji; Hua Tan of Guangling, Interior Minister of Lujiang, and Ge Hong and Gan Zhuo of Danyang all raised troops in response to Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon former attendant censor He Xun raised troops at Kuaiji. Hua Tan of Guangling, interior minister of Lujiang, and Ge Hong and Gan Zhuo of Danyang all raised troops in response to Gu Mi.

sentences.zh: 玘，處之子；
